mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS has declined over the past month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% and is rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a weakening demand environment that reduces corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term in a regression model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising labor force participation rate (PAYEMS growth) signals tight labor market conditions that may lead to inflationary pressures and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth is positive, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates robust economic activity and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO has increased over the past three months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 5.0% and is accelerating, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary policy responses, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 5.0% and accelerating, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a tightening monetary policy amid high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are rising, or the interaction term in a regression model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of strong economic growth (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annually), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending supply shock that reduces corporate output and profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth is above 2.0% annually and INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.
